1.text: Kāf, Hā, Yā, ʿAyn, Ṣād.<sup foot_note="227189">1</sup>

2.text: [This is] a mention of the mercy of your Lord to His servant Zechariah

3.text: When he called to his Lord a private call [i.e., supplication].

4.text: He said, "My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened, and my head has filled<sup foot_note="227190">1</sup> with white, and never have I been in my supplication to You, my Lord, unhappy [i.e., disappointed].

footnotes.227190: - Literally, "ignited."  The spread of white hair throughout the head is likened to that of fire in the bush.

5.text: And indeed, I fear the successors<sup foot_note="227191">1</sup> after me, and my wife has been barren, so give me from Yourself an heir

footnotes.227191: - Those relatives from the father's side who would inherit religious authority.

6.text: Who will inherit me<sup foot_note="227192">1</sup> and inherit from the family of Jacob. And make him, my Lord, pleasing [to You]."

footnotes.227192: - Inherit from me religious knowledge and prophethood.

7.text: [He was told],<sup foot_note="227193">1</sup> "O Zechariah, indeed We give you good tidings of a boy whose name will be John. We have not assigned to any before [this] name."

footnotes.227193: - By Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) through the angels.

8.text: He said, "My Lord, how will I have a boy when my wife has been barren and I have reached extreme old age?"

9.text: [An angel] said, "Thus [it will be]; your Lord says, 'It is easy for Me, for I created you before, while you were nothing.'"

10.text: [Zechariah] said, "My Lord, make for me a sign." He said, "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three nights, [being] sound."<sup foot_note="227194">1</sup>

11.text: So he came out to his people from the prayer chamber and signaled to them to exalt [Allāh] in the morning and afternoon.

12.text: [Allāh said], "O John, take the Scripture [i.e., adhere to it] with determination." And We gave him judgement [while yet] a boy

13.text: And affection from Us and purity, and he was fearing of Allāh

14.text: And dutiful to his parents, and he was not a disobedient tyrant.

15.text: And peace be upon him the day he was born and the day he dies and the day he is raised alive.

16.text: And mention, [O Muḥammad], in the Book [the story of] Mary, when she withdrew from her family to a place toward the east.

17.text: And she took, in seclusion from them, a screen. Then We sent to her Our Angel [i.e., Gabriel], and he represented himself to her as a well-proportioned man.

18.text: She said, "Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, [so leave me], if you should be fearing of Allāh."

19.text: He said, "I am only the messenger of your Lord to give you [news of] a pure boy [i.e., son]."

20.text: She said, "How can I have a boy while no man has touched me and I have not been unchaste?"

21.text: He said, "Thus [it will be]; your Lord says, 'It is easy for Me, and We will make him a sign to the people and a mercy from Us. And it is a matter [already] decreed.'"

22.text: So she conceived him, and she withdrew with him to a remote place.

23.text: And the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree. She said, "Oh, I wish I had died before this and was in oblivion, forgotten."

24.text: But he<sup foot_note="227195">1</sup> called her from below her, "Do not grieve; your Lord has provided beneath you a stream.

footnotes.227195: - There is a difference of opinion among scholars as to whether "he" refers to the baby or to the angel.

25.text: And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you ripe, fresh dates.

26.text: So eat and drink and be contented. And if you see from among humanity anyone, say, 'Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful abstention, so I will not speak today to [any] man.'"

27.text: Then she brought him to her people, carrying him. They said, "O Mary, you have certainly done a thing unprecedented.

28.text: O sister [i.e., descendant] of Aaron, your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother unchaste."

29.text: So she pointed to him. They said, "How can we speak to one who is in the cradle a child?"

30.text: [Jesus] said, "Indeed, I am the servant of Allāh. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet.

31.text: And He has made me blessed wherever I am and has enjoined upon me prayer and zakāh as long as I remain alive

32.text: And [made me] dutiful to my mother, and He has not made me a wretched tyrant.

33.text: And peace is on me the day I was born and the day I will die and the day I am raised alive."

34.text: That is Jesus, the son of Mary - the word of truth about which they are in dispute.

35.text: It is not [befitting] for Allāh to take a son; exalted is He!<sup foot_note="227196">1</sup> When He decrees an affair, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.

footnotes.227196: - i.e., far removed is He from any such need.

36.text: [Jesus said], "And indeed, Allāh is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. That is a straight path."

37.text: Then the factions differed [concerning Jesus] from among them, so woe to those who disbelieved - from the scene of a tremendous Day.

38.text: How [clearly] they will hear and see the Day they come to Us, but the wrongdoers today are in clear error.

39.text: And warn them, [O Muḥammad], of the Day of Regret, when the matter will be concluded;<sup foot_note="227197">1</sup> and [yet], they are in [a state of] heedlessness, and they do not believe.

40.text: Indeed, it is We who will inherit the earth and whoever is on it, and to Us they will be returned.

41.text: And mention in the Book [the story of] Abraham. Indeed, he was a man of truth and a prophet.

42.text: [Mention] when he said to his father, "O my father, why do you worship that which does not hear and does not see and will not benefit you at all?

43.text: O my father, indeed there has come to me of knowledge that which has not come to you, so follow me; I will guide you to an even path.

44.text: O my father, do not worship [i.e., obey] Satan. Indeed Satan has ever been, to the Most Merciful, disobedient.

45.text: O my father, indeed I fear that there will touch you a punishment from the Most Merciful so you would be to Satan a companion [in Hellfire]."

46.text: [His father] said, "Have you no desire for my gods, O Abraham? If you do not desist, I will surely stone you, so avoid me a prolonged time."

47.text: [Abraham] said, "Peace [i.e., safety] will be upon you.<sup foot_note="227198">1</sup> I will ask forgiveness for you of my Lord. Indeed, He is ever gracious to me.

footnotes.227198: - Meaning "You are secure" or "I will not harm you."

48.text: And I will leave you and those you invoke other than Allāh and will invoke<sup foot_note="227199">1</sup> my Lord. I expect that I will not be in invocation to my Lord unhappy [i.e., disappointed]."

49.text: So when he had left them and those they worshipped other than Allāh, We gave him Isaac and Jacob, and each [of them] We made a prophet.

50.text: And We gave them of Our mercy, and We made for them a mention [i.e., reputation] of high honor.

51.text: And mention in the Book, Moses. Indeed, he was chosen, and he was a messenger and a prophet.<sup foot_note="227200">1</sup>

footnotes.227200: - A messenger (rasūl) is one who was charged by Allāh to reform society.  A prophet (nabī) is one who received revelation from Allāh, the latter being more numerous than the former.

52.text: And We called him from the side of the mount<sup foot_note="227201">1</sup> at [his] right and brought him near, confiding [to him].

53.text: And We gave him out of Our mercy his brother Aaron as a prophet.

54.text: And mention in the Book, Ishmael. Indeed, he was true to his promise, and he was a messenger and a prophet.

55.text: And he used to enjoin on his people prayer and zakāh and was to his Lord pleasing [i.e., accepted by Him].

56.text: And mention in the Book, Idrees. Indeed, he was a man of truth and a prophet.

57.text: And We raised him to a high station.

58.text: Those were the ones upon whom Allāh bestowed favor from among the prophets of the descendants of Adam and of those We carried [in the ship] with Noah, and of the descendants of Abraham and Israel [i.e., Jacob], and of those whom We guided and chose. When the verses of the Most Merciful were recited to them, they fell in prostration and weeping.

59.text: But there came after them successors [i.e., later generations] who neglected prayer and pursued desires; so they are going to meet evil<sup foot_note="227202">1</sup> -

footnotes.227202: - Described as a valley in Hell or may be rendered "the consequence of error."

60.text: Except those who repent, believe and do righteousness; for those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged at all.

61.text: [Therein are] gardens of perpetual residence which the Most Merciful has promised His servants in the unseen. Indeed, His promise has ever been eminent.<sup foot_note="227203">1</sup>

footnotes.227203: - Literally, "that to which all will come."

62.text: They will not hear therein any ill speech - only [greetings of] peace - and they will have their provision therein, morning and afternoon.

63.text: That is Paradise, which We give as inheritance to those of Our servants who were fearing of Allāh.

64.text: [Gabriel said],<sup foot_note="227204">1</sup> "And we [angels] descend not except by the order of your Lord. To Him belongs that before us and that behind us and what is in between. And never is your Lord forgetful -

footnotes.227204: - In answer to the Prophet's wish that Gabriel would visit him more often.

65.text: Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them - so worship Him and have patience for His worship. Do you know of any similarity to Him?"

66.text: And man [i.e., the disbeliever] says, "When I have died, am I going to be brought forth alive?"

67.text: Does man not remember that We created him before, while he was nothing?

68.text: So by your Lord, We will surely gather them and the devils; then We will bring them to be present around Hell upon their knees.<sup foot_note="227205">1</sup>

footnotes.227205: - i.e., fallen on their knees from terror or dragged there unwillingly on their knees.

69.text: Then We will surely extract from every sect those of them who were worst against the Most Merciful in insolence.

70.text: Then, surely it is We who are most knowing of those most worthy of burning therein.

71.text: And there is none of you except he will come to it.<sup foot_note="227206">1</sup> This is upon your Lord an inevitability decreed.

footnotes.227206: - i.e., be exposed to it.  However, the people of Paradise will not be harmed thereby.

72.text: Then We will save those who feared Allāh and leave the wrongdoers within it, on their knees.

73.text: And when Our verses are recited to them as clear evidences, those who disbelieve say to those who believe, "Which of [our] two parties is best in position and best in association?"<sup foot_note="227207">1</sup>

74.text: And how many a generation have We destroyed before them who were better in possessions and [outward] appearance?

75.text: Say, "Whoever is in error - let the Most Merciful extend for him an extension [in wealth and time] until, when they see that which they were promised - either punishment [in this world] or the Hour [of resurrection] - they will come to know who is worst in position and weaker in soldiers."

76.text: And Allāh increases those who were guided, in guidance, and the enduring good deeds are better to your Lord<sup foot_note="227208">1</sup> for reward and better for recourse.

footnotes.227208: - i.e., in the sight or evaluation of Allāh.

77.text: Then, have you seen he who disbelieved in Our verses and said, "I will surely be given wealth and children [in the next life]"?

78.text: Has he looked into the unseen, or has he taken from the Most Merciful a promise?

79.text: No! We will record what he says and extend [i.e., increase] for him from the punishment extensively.

80.text: And We will inherit him [in] what he mentions,<sup foot_note="227209">1</sup> and he will come to Us alone.

footnotes.227209: - Instead of giving him wealth and children in the Hereafter, Allāh will take from him those he had in worldly life at the time of his death.

81.text: And they have taken besides Allāh [false] deities that they would be for them [a source of] honor.

82.text: No! They [i.e., those "gods"] will deny their worship of them and will be against them opponents [on the Day of Judgement].

83.text: Do you not see that We have sent the devils upon the disbelievers, inciting them [to evil] with [constant] incitement?

84.text: So be not impatient over them. We only count out [i.e., allow] to them a [limited] number.<sup foot_note="227210">1</sup>

footnotes.227210: - Of breaths, of days, or of evil deeds.

85.text: On the Day We will gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation

86.text: And will drive the criminals to Hell in thirst

87.text: None will have [power of] intercession except he who had taken from the Most Merciful a covenant.<sup foot_note="227211">1</sup>

footnotes.227211: - Not to worship other than Him.

88.text: And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken [for Himself] a son."

89.text: You have done an atrocious thing.

90.text: The heavens almost rupture therefrom and the earth splits open and the mountains collapse in devastation

91.text: That they attribute to the Most Merciful a son.

92.text: And it is not appropriate for the Most Merciful that He should take a son.

93.text: There is no one in the heavens and earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant.

94.text: He has enumerated them and counted them a [full] counting.

95.text: And all of them are coming to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone.

96.text: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection.<sup foot_note="227212">1</sup>

footnotes.227212: - From Himself and from among each other.

97.text: So, [O Muḥammad], We have only made it [i.e., the Qur’ān] easy in your tongue [i.e., the Arabic language] that you may give good tidings thereby to the righteous and warn thereby a hostile people.

98.text: And how many have We destroyed before them of generations? Do you perceive of them anyone or hear from them a sound?
